headlines.summary: Disney shares ticked higher Tuesday after the media giant reported quarterly results that beat analyst expectations.
headlines.article_text: Stocks moving the most today: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Cheng Xin | Getty Images Disney shares ticked higher in early trading after the media giant reported quarterly results that beat analyst expectations. Nvidia rose as well, as the chipmaker tried to recoup some of its losses from Monday. Traders also awaited the company's latest earnings report, due out after the market closes Tuesday. Follow along as CNBC highlights the biggest stock market moves of the day. 1 Hour Ago Nucor upgraded to overweight with higher price target at Morgan Stanley Charlotte, N.C.-based steelmaker Nucor won an upgrade to overweight from equal weight, and an increased price target of $310 from $300, at Morgan Stanley by analysts led by Carlos De Alba, who said Nucor will benefit from stronger free cash flow as capital investment spending declines. The Wall Street investment bank, which also raised its price target on Steel Dynamics to $270 from $260, lifted its near term steel price forecasts due to tight supplies probably keeping hot rolled coil prices above $1,100 per short ton in the first half of 2027. Nucor shares have soared 57% in 2026 and about 72% over the past year Both Nucor and Steel Dynamics are about 1% higher in early trading Tuesday. — Scott Schnipper 2 Hours Ago JPMorgan downgrades Tyson Foods after sharp rally JPMorgan downgraded Tyson Foods to neutral from overweight, saying its 23% rally over two months leaves limited upside. The bank raised the price target to $65, implying about 2% upside from Monday's close. Tyson Foods - stock price Tyson Foods reported fiscal fourth quarter and fiscal 2026 results on Monday, projecting sales declining 3.5% to 5.5% and adjusted operating income of $1.7 billion to $2.15 billion. JPMorgan analyst Thomas Palmer sees beef profits recovering and chicken conditions stabilizing, but flagged higher annual feed costs and weaker free cash flow ahead. "We are encouraged by these developments but also believe that the stock price recovery better reflects underlying fundamentals," the analyst said. — Deena Zaidi 3 Hours Ago Data center and infrastructure stocks rally Data center and infrastructure stocks rallied after a Reuters report , citing people briefed on the matter, said the Trump administration plans to block imports of Chinese data center equipment. Shares of photonic technology companies rallied following the news. Here are some of the moves. Coherent shares rally 11% Applied Optoelectronics shares rally 8.6% Lumentum shares 5.6% Coherent — Sarah Min 3 Hours Ago Sellas Life Sciences rises after cancer vaccine trial results Shares of biopharmaceutical company Sellas Life Sciences rose more than 7% after it reported positive trial results for one of its immunotherapeutic cancer vaccines. Galinpepimut-S, which is designed to treat acute myeloid leukemia, in a phase 3 trial met its primary endpoint for overall survival. The company added it reduced the risk of death by 41% and showed no new safety risks compared to previous trials. Sellas Life Sciences 3-month. — Davis Giangiulio 4 Hours Ago Deutsche Bank shares slip after internal files leak points to suspicious activity at bank Shares for Deutsche Bank fell over 2.5% after whistleblowers leaked about 15 million internal files from the bank, exposing alleged, systemic failures and suspicious payments linked to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. dbf — Ananya Chetia 4 Hours Ago Intel slides after Nvidia cuts its stake Intel slipped after Nvidia disclosed that it cut its stake in the company. Nvidia said in a regulatory filing that it trimmed its stake by 25% in the quarter ending Sept. 30, selling nearly $5.5 billion in shares. The move lowers Nvidia's holding in Intel to 161 million shares from 215 million. — Darla Mercado 4 Hours Ago Nvidia shares rise ahead of earnings Nvidia shares gained 1% ahead of the chipmaker's earnings, and following days of decline amid the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO. Huang resigned from Nvidia, the company's board announced on Thursday, following reports that he had a relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy. Huang told employees he had an affair in an email on Nov. 8. Nvidia — Kai Nicol-Schwarz and Sarah Min 4 Hours Ago Home Depot falls after CEO change Home Depot shares were down nearly 2% after the home improvement giant announced Richard McPhail would take over as CEO from Ted Decker, effective next week. Decker, who will remain as chairman, had been on medical leave since August. HD 5-day chart — Fred Imbert 4 Hours Ago Disney ticks higher on earnings beat Disney reported fiscal fourth-quarter results that beat the Street , sending the stock higher by nearly 2%. The media giant earned an adjusted $1.77 per share on revenue of $25.95 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG expected a profit of $1.67 per share on revenue of $25.18 billion. The company also announced it's targeting $3 billion in cost cuts by fiscal 2029. DIS 5-day chart — Fred Imbert

headlines.article_text: Home Depot (HD) Q3 earnings 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Home Depot named Richard McPhail as its new CEO effective next week. McPhail currently serves as CFO. CEO Ted Decker had been on a temporary medical leave of absence but has since returned, according to Home Depot. The company made the announcement as it posted earnings and revenue that beat expectations. In this article HD Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Home Depot store logo sign is seen in Chicago, Illinois, United States, on August 3, 2026. Marcin Golba | Nurphoto | Getty Images Home Depot on Tuesday announced its Chief Financial Officer Richard McPhail will become CEO of the company, replacing Ted Decker, effective next week. Alongside McPhail's appointment, Home Depot said Ann-Marie Campbell, currently senior executive vice president of U.S. stores and operations, will become president and chief operating officer. Jordan Broggi has been chosen as CFO to replace McPhail. Decker, CEO since 2022, had been on temporary medical leave since August. The company said on Tuesday that Decker has returned from leave but is now stepping down from his role. He will continue to serve as chair of the board of directors, the company said. "I'm glad to be back and grateful for the support I received," Decker told analysts on Tuesday. "The board and I have agreed that now is the right time to move to the next phase of our succession plan." McPhail has been with the company since 2005, holding multiple executive roles. "We're not going to change course," McPhail told CNBC's Becky Quick. He said the company will continue to lean into winning professional shoppers like contractors and using AI tools to encourage sales. McPhail added that while the company faces more challenges now than it did at the start of the year, it is still winning share of the home improvement market. Home Depot has been pressured by a sluggish housing market, higher mortgage rates and a more cautious consumer. Still, the company has previously said it's seen resilience among its pro shoppers who are still shopping for their home improvement projects. Shares of Home Depot sank more than 3% following the announcement and the retailer's fiscal third-quarter results. The CEO change came as the home improvement retailer posted quarterly earnings and revenue that beat analysts' expectations. The company said comparable sales rose 2.2% during the period, compared with estimates of up 1.8%, according to StreetAccount. Here's how Home Depot performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: $3.86 adjusted vs. $3.84 expected Revenue: $43.4 billion vs. $42.80 billion expected The company reported net income of $3.71 billion, or $3.72 per share, compared with $3.60 billion, or $3.62 per share, the year prior. Excluding one-time items, Home Depot reported adjusted earnings per share of $3.86. Revenue rose 4.9% compared to the year-ago period. "We also are confident that we are taking material share from the market and from competition," McPhail said on the call with analysts. In the third quarter, the company said online comparable sales grew around 13%, which marked its sixth straight quarter of double-digit positive growth for the metric. The company said it saw positive comparable sales numbers in 13 out of 16 of its merchandising departments, including notable strength in the power department, which posted double-digit percentage growth. For the full year, Home Depot said it expects total sales to rise roughly 4.5%, the top end of its previously provided range. It also anticipates comparable sales will grow around 1.4%, compared with an outlook of flat to a 2% increase. Home Depot added it expects adjusted earnings per share to rise 2% this year, compared with prior guidance of flat to a 4% increase.
